title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Evan Cho
release_notes: Add autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, introduce quantization profile defaults, and expose unit-econ simulation tooling. Improvements reduce per-token cost by ~12% on average across representative workloads; safe rollout via canary and config flags.
body: Context: Customers running high-throughput inference hit unit economics limits due to conservative batching/caching defaults and a lack of standardized quantization profiles. This PR wires together three pieces: 1) safer defaults for batching and KV caching that improve throughput without compromising 99th percentile latency SLOs, 2) a set of quantization profiles (per-model-family defaults) and a lightweight runtime selector, and 3) developer-facing unit-econ tooling to simulate expected cost/latency tradeoffs for a given workload so operators can pick sensible defaults. Summary of changes: commits touch the runtime batching scheduler, KV cache parameters, model registry (quant profiles), API surface for setting per-route autotune policy, and a new CLI tool redwood-uecon that runs simulations against historical trace samples. Key results: end-to-end integration test suite added; internal perf bench shows ~12% median per-token cost reduction, 7% P99 latency impact (within SLO), and 15% TPU/GPU utilization improvement for majority of mixed workloads. Rollout plan: feature gated under config.autotune.cost_optimization (disabled by default for private installs), staged canary on 5% of traffic with auto-roll back on latency regressions, dashboards and alerts added in the Console. Checklist: - Motivation and design doc linked (Linear ENG-1982) - Unit and integration tests added - Manual perf runs against benchmark-lab and perf-canary - Canary/rollout config included - Docs updated in redwood-docs How to review: focus on runtime changes (serving/runtime/scheduler.go), model registry additions (redwood-model-registry/quant_profiles.yaml), and the unit-econ CLI (redwood-tools/uecon/*). Pay attention to default values in config/defaults.go and the autotune selection logic in serving/runtime/autotune_manager.go. Backwards compatibility: existing per-route configs continue to take precedence; quant profiles are additive and must be opted in via model metadata or the route config. Related: ENG-2041 (quant profile onboarding), SUP-734 (customer cases driving defaults). Merge: squash merge after approvals and green CI.
commits: feat(runtime): introduce autoscaling-aware batching policy and per-route batch limits
perf(runtime): tune KV cache eviction/retention defaults, add metrics for cache hit-eviction
feat(registry): add quantization profile definitions and selector logic
feat(cli): add redwood-uecon tool to simulate unit economics from traces
test: add integration tests for autotune end-to-end in perf-canary
docs: document new defaults and rollout guide in redwood-docs
changed_files: serving/runtime/scheduler.go - add policy hooks and new default batch window
serving/runtime/kv_cache.go - adjust retention and eviction thresholds, add cache metrics
serving/runtime/autotune_manager.go - selection logic for batch/cache/quant profiles
redwood-model-registry/quant_profiles.yaml - profiles for llama-family, mixtral, stablelm, tiny models
redwood-tools/uecon/main.go - CLI and simulator for cost/latency tradeoffs
ci/pipelines/autotune.yml - CI job for perf tests
review_comments: Laura Chen: The new batching window default looks aggressive for short-sequence chat loads. Can we add guardrails to auto-reduce batch windows when latency spikes?
Evan Cho: Added a reactive limiter in autotune_manager that reduces batch window if P99 > config.autotune.latency_threshold; also included tests.
Miguel Alvarez: Quant profiles look good, please ensure the selector prefers model-specific profile over family defaults (edge case: user-provided weights).
Evan Cho: Selector now checks model.metadata.quant_profile then route overrides then family defaults. Documented precedence in model registry README.
Priya Shah: Can you add telemetry that surfaces per-route unit-econ delta pre/post rollout to Console?
Evan Cho: Added telemetry (cost.delta_per_route, latency.delta_per_route) and dashboard panels; included dashboards in PR.
QA Bot: flake detected in integration test autotune_integration_test.go line 132; rerunning CI recommended.
Evan Cho: Fixed test flake by adding a polling helper and increased timeout; CI rerun passed.
merge_outcome_notes: Merged after 3 approvals. Canary ran for 48h with no regressions; feature enabled for 5% production traffic, scheduled rollout after monitoring window.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature via config.autotune.cost_optimization=true in release notes to rollout
Use redwood-uecon simulate --trace <s3-path> to validate cost impact before enabling
